sides.text: S3 Standard
Frequently accessed data; no retrieval fee, no minimum duration
S3 Intelligent-Tiering
Automatically moves objects between access tiers based on use; small monitoring fee, no retrieval fees

more.text: Best when access patterns are unknown or changing.

sides.head: Example
sides.text: Access patterns are unknown and unpredictable. Which class minimizes cost with no retrieval fees?

sides.head: Answer
sides.text: S3 Intelligent-Tiering

more.text: Automatic tier movement

sides.text: S3 Standard-IA and One Zone-IA
Infrequent access with retrieval fees; 30-day minimum, 128 KB minimum billable size

more.text: One Zone-IA stores in one AZ (cheaper, less resilient).

sides.text: S3 Glacier classes
Instant Retrieval (milliseconds, 90-day minimum), Flexible Retrieval (minutes to hours, 90 days), Deep Archive (12–48 hours, 180 days)

more.text: Cheapest per GB for archives.

sides.head: Example
sides.text: Compliance archive accessed once a year, retrieval within 12 hours is fine, lowest cost

sides.head: Answer
sides.text: S3 Glacier Deep Archive

more.text: 180-day minimum storage duration

sides.text: Glacier retrieval options

Flexible Retrieval:
Expedited 1–5 minutes
Standard 3–5 hours
Bulk 5–12 hours

more.text: Deep Archive: Standard within 12 hours, Bulk within 48 hours.

sides.text: S3 lifecycle policies
Transition objects between classes and expire them after set days

more.text: Example: Standard, then Standard-IA at 30 days, Glacier at 90, delete at 365.

sides.head: Example
sides.text: Logs are read often for 30 days, rarely until 1 year, then deleted. Design?

sides.head: Answer
sides.text: Standard for 30 days, Glacier Flexible Retrieval after, expire at 365 days

more.text: Lifecycle rules automate transitions

sides.text: S3 Requester Pays
The requester pays request and transfer costs instead of the bucket owner

more.text: Useful for sharing large datasets.

sides.head: Example
sides.text: A research bucket should bill downloaders for transfer

sides.head: Answer
sides.text: Enable Requester Pays

more.text: The requester must be authenticated

sides.text: EBS volume cost choices

gp3 is cheaper than gp2 for equal performance
st1 for throughput-heavy sequential workloads
sc1 for the coldest data

more.text: Delete unattached volumes and old snapshots.

sides.text: Storage tiering
Hot data on SSD or S3 Standard, warm on IA classes, cold on Glacier
Efficient uploads
Use multipart upload for large objects, batch small files, and S3 Transfer Acceleration only when it helps
Low-cost data transfer to AWS
Transfers into AWS are free; choose DataSync, Snow family, or Direct Connect by volume and time
Storage auto scaling
S3 and EFS grow automatically; RDS storage autoscaling raises allocated storage on demand
Backup and archival choices
AWS Backup with lifecycle to cold storage, EBS snapshots (incremental), S3 Glacier for long retention
EFS cost features
EFS Infrequent Access and Archive classes with lifecycle management; One Zone storage classes
FSx cost features
FSx deduplication and compression; HDD storage for lower cost on Windows file servers
Choosing the cheapest storage service

S3 is the cheapest for objects
EFS costs more than EBS per GB for shared files
instance store is included in instance price

Visualize, filter, and forecast costs and usage; right-sizing recommendations
AWS Budgets
Set cost, usage, and reservation budgets with alerts and actions

sides.text: Alert when monthly spend is forecast to exceed $5,000

sides.head: Answer
sides.text: AWS Budgets with a forecast alert

more.text: Alerts by email or SNS

sides.text: AWS Cost and Usage Report (CUR)
Most detailed billing data delivered to S3, queried with Athena
Cost allocation tags
Tag resources and activate tags in billing to attribute costs to teams and projects

sides.head: Example
sides.text: Charge costs back to each team

sides.head: Answer
sides.text: Tag resources and activate cost allocation tags

more.text: Visible in Cost Explorer and CUR

sides.text: Consolidated billing
Organizations combine account bills for volume discounts and shared Savings Plans or Reserved Instances
AWS Compute Optimizer and Trusted Advisor
Compute Optimizer recommends right sizes using metrics. Trusted Advisor checks cost, security, and limits
AWS Pricing Calculator
Estimate costs before building; Billing and Cost Management shows actuals
On-Demand instances
Pay per second with no commitment; best for short, unpredictable workloads
Reserved Instances

1 or 3 year commitment for large discounts (up to about 72%)
Standard or Convertible
zonal capacity reservation optional

more.text: Pay all upfront, partial, or none.

sides.head: Example
sides.text: A database runs 24/7 for the next 3 years

sides.head: Answer
sides.text: Reserved Instances or a Savings Plan

more.text: Steady use qualifies for deep discounts

sides.text: Savings Plans
Commit to a spend per hour for 1 or 3 years. Compute Savings Plans also cover Fargate and Lambda; EC2 Instance Savings Plans give the deepest discounts for a family and Region

sides.head: Example
sides.text: Spend commitment that also covers Fargate and Lambda usage

sides.head: Answer
sides.text: Compute Savings Plan

more.text: EC2 Instance Savings Plans do not cover them

sides.text: Spot Instances
Up to 90% off spare capacity; can be reclaimed with a 2-minute warning

more.text: Use for stateless, fault-tolerant, flexible batch, CI, and big data tasks.

sides.head: Example
sides.text: A fault-tolerant nightly batch job must run at the lowest cost

sides.head: Answer
sides.text: Spot Instances

more.text: Interruptions are acceptable

sides.text: Spot Fleet and Auto Scaling mixed instances
Diversify instance types and AZs; mix On-Demand base with Spot
Dedicated Hosts and Instances
Single-tenant hardware for licensing or compliance; the most expensive option
Capacity Reservations
Reserve capacity in an AZ at On-Demand prices; combine with Savings Plans for discounts
Right-sizing
Match instance family and size to measured CPU, memory, and network use

more.text: Consider Graviton for better price-performance.

sides.head: Example
sides.text: Instances average 10% CPU and low memory use. What now?

sides.head: Answer
sides.text: Right-size to a smaller family or size

more.text: Use Compute Optimizer recommendations

sides.text: EC2 hibernation
Saves RAM to EBS so instances resume quickly; useful for slow-start applications and cost savings when idle
Lambda vs EC2 vs Fargate cost
Lambda for spiky or short tasks (pay per use). EC2 for steady heavy load. Fargate for containers without servers
Scheduling non-production
Stop dev and test instances outside business hours with Instance Scheduler or Auto Scaling schedules

sides.head: Example
sides.text: Dev servers sit idle every night and weekend

sides.head: Answer
sides.text: Schedule start and stop times

more.text: Saves more than 60% of the hours

sides.text: Load balancer cost choices
One ALB can serve many apps with host or path rules, saving the cost of several load balancers
AWS Outposts and Snowball Edge
Hybrid compute at on-premises or disconnected sites; edge processing reduces data transfer
Required availability by workload
Production: multi-AZ and reserved capacity. Non-production: single AZ, Spot, and scheduled shutdown
DynamoDB vs RDS cost
DynamoDB on-demand suits spiky key-value access. RDS or Aurora suits relational workloads with joins
Aurora Serverless
Capacity scales automatically and can pause (v1) or scale to a minimum (v2); good for variable workloads

sides.head: Example
sides.text: A database used only a few hours a day with unpredictable load

sides.head: Answer
sides.text: Aurora Serverless

more.text: Pay for capacity actually used

sides.text: RDS Reserved Instances
Discounts for steady database usage with a 1 or 3 year term
Database backups and retention
Automated backups are free up to the database size; manual snapshots persist until deleted

more.text: Choose retention (1 to 35 days) and snapshot frequency to match RPO and cost.

sides.text: Caching to cut database cost
ElastiCache and read replicas reduce load so a smaller primary suffices
Choosing database types for cost
Timestream for time series, Redshift for columnar analytics, S3 plus Athena for rarely queried data
Database migration cost
DMS has low cost; homogeneous migrations are simpler than heterogeneous ones needing SCT
DynamoDB cost levers
TTL to expire items, on-demand vs provisioned with auto scaling, Standard-IA table class for rarely read data, reserved capacity
AWS data transfer pricing rules
Inbound from the internet is free. Outbound to the internet is charged. Between AZs and between Regions is charged. Within the same AZ over private IP is free

more.text: Keep chatty components in the same AZ when possible.

sides.head: Example
sides.text: Which traffic is free?

sides.head: Answer
sides.text: Inbound from the internet and within an AZ over private IPs

more.text: Cross-AZ, cross-Region, and internet egress are charged

sides.text: NAT gateway cost
Hourly charge plus per-GB processing; one per AZ for resilience but one shared NAT is cheaper for non-production

more.text: NAT instances can be cheaper at low volume but need management.

sides.head: Example
sides.text: A dev environment uses three NAT gateways across three AZs

sides.head: Answer
sides.text: Use a single NAT gateway to cut cost

more.text: Production keeps one per AZ for resilience

sides.text: VPC endpoints to save cost
Gateway endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB are free and avoid NAT data processing charges

sides.head: Example
sides.text: Private instances send terabytes to S3 through a NAT gateway

sides.head: Answer
sides.text: Add an S3 gateway endpoint

more.text: It removes NAT data processing charges

sides.text: VPC peering vs Transit Gateway cost
Peering has no hourly charge but does not scale for many VPCs. Transit Gateway charges per attachment and per GB

more.text: Choose by number of VPCs.

sides.text: Direct Connect vs VPN vs internet
Direct Connect lowers per-GB egress and gives consistent performance but has port-hour fees. VPN is cheap and quick. Internet is cheapest but variable

sides.head: Example
sides.text: Large steady transfer between on-premises and AWS should cost less per GB

sides.head: Answer
sides.text: AWS Direct Connect

more.text: Lower egress rates than internet

sides.text: CloudFront cost benefits
Caching reduces origin load and data transfer out from the origin; edge egress is cheaper than S3 or EC2 egress
Route 53 and DNS cost
Alias queries to AWS resources are free; use them instead of CNAMEs where possible
Throttling strategy
API Gateway usage plans, WAF rate-based rules, and SQS buffering smooth load and protect budgets
Network bandwidth allocation
Match VPN count (about 1.25 Gbps per tunnel) and Direct Connect port speed to need
Region choice and transfer
Prices vary by Region; keep compute near data to avoid cross-Region transfer

Break-even utilization?

more.text:
Reserved annual cost = 0.06 × 8,760 = $525.60
On-Demand cost at utilization u: 0.10 × 8,760 × u
Set equal: u = 0.06 / 0.10 = 0.60
